arch_delta.definition: ARM r8gd.8xlarge vep-rs median divided by x86 r8id.8xlarge vep-rs median, per cell; >1 means x86 is faster.

clone_manifest_note: clones[] holds one entry per clone per engine per arch. Entries of an engine measured in this sweep are read from that clone's terminal marker (instance id, inventory digest, binary digest verified against the pin). Suite-scoped re-measurement, each entry naming the suites its clone measured. fastVEP: s07, s08 measured in this sweep on 40 fresh clones; the s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s05m, s06, s06m clones imported from that engine's campaign, sweep-20260918T224520Z; Perl VEP: s07, s08 measured in this sweep on 40 fresh clones; the s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s06 clones imported from that engine's campaign, sweep-20260918T224520Z.
clone_manifest_supplementary_note: 8 entries carry role=sv_scoring, the clones outside the main cohort from which the published s07, s08 adjusted F1 is read (vep-rs: clone-21 arm64, clone-22 arm64, clone-21 x86_64, clone-22 x86_64; fastVEP: clone-21 arm64, clone-22 arm64, clone-21 x86_64, clone-22 x86_64); their raw F1 and tuple counts equal the main cohort's (fastvep_cross_clone_determinism.main_clones_raw_identical here; sv_scoring_note in the concordance record).
concurrency_note: Clones launch in staggered batches and run concurrently, up to 20 per engine per arch. Each clone self-terminates the moment its results upload; there is no fleet-wide wait barrier.
cross_engine_ratios_note: Per-cell form of speedups_p1 and speedups_sv: fastVEP median divided by vep-rs median, and Perl median divided by vep-rs median, per sites-only cell per arch, computed from the medians in per_cell_aggregates.
dataset_inventory_sha256_note: Dataset parity holds within every engine measured in this sweep, read from each clone's COMPLETE marker and inventory.sha256: fastVEP: all 40 clones measured this sweep (s07, s08) rolled 41797ac1 on both arches; its reused clones' digest is on record in their own campaign's entries; Perl VEP: all 40 clones measured this sweep (s07, s08) rolled cde7eee3 on both arches; its reused clones' digest is on record in their own campaign's entries; vep-rs: all 40 clones rolled 15c55e95 on both arches. The per-engine values differ because each engine syncs only the read-side artifacts it consumes.
fastvep_cross_clone_determinism_note: fastVEP's raw and adjusted F1 and its three tuple counts are identical on every clone that scored a suite, read here from each clone's report under the sweep that measured the suite (clones_reporting per suite; the two architectures pooled, F1 being architecture-independent), and equal the row manuscript/data/f1_observations_fastvep.csv carries. Where a suite's published values come from supplementary clones (source under svscore), main_clones_raw_identical counts the main clones whose raw F1 and tuple counts equal theirs.
fastvep_measured_note: fastVEP v0.3.0 (ARM 6d83c5bc, x86 e123fbc0) was measured in sweep-20260918T224520Z on both architectures; its structural-variant cells (s07, s08) are from this sweep (sweep-20260920T012411Z), whose structural-variant inputs differ from that campaign's (selective_remeasurement), with binaries byte-identical to that campaign's; its other wall-time rows in wall_times.csv and its SNP and indel concordance rows in manuscript/data/f1_observations_fastvep.csv carry sweep_id=sweep-20260918T224520Z. fastVEP F1 is architecture-independent; the SV comparator maps fastVEP's symbolic alleles to VEP's Sequence Ontology class names before scoring (compare_sv_concordance.py --scored-engine fastvep).
fastvep_pin_note: fastVEP is pinned to the citable v0.3.0 release (ARM 6d83c5bc, x86 e123fbc0), built from the upstream v0.3.0 tag. Wall time and concordance were both measured at this version in sweep-20260918T224520Z, so the fastVEP columns of every table share one campaign.
fork_note: vep-rs and Perl VEP both run --fork 16 --buffer_size 5000 on the 32-vCPU hosts; fastVEP parallelizes internally with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=16. At --fork 16 the container cgroup memory.peak of Perl VEP on the sites-only inputs is at most 17.7 GiB (gnomad_v4.1_chr21_sites_only; manuscript/data/perl_bench.csv). Every engine runs its SV cells (s07/s08) per VCF at the same --fork 16: run_clone_measurement.sh forwards $FORK on every engine's SV branch, and vep-rs fork-invariance is gated by test_annotate_batch_fork_1_matches_fork_4 in crates/vep-cli/src/runner.rs plus the harness tests that assert every engine's SV cell takes the same --fork and that vep-rs output is fork-independent, so the SV ratios in speedups_sv compare like-for-like invocations.
methodology_note: 20 fresh clones per engine per architecture, each self-bootstrapped from the stock AL2023 base AMI and each contributing exactly one cold-discarded warmup plus one timed measurement per cell. Per-cell statistics are the distribution across those 20 cross-instance samples, computed per architecture; the paper reports the ARM-vs-x86 delta rather than a single blended number.
n_clones_per_arch_note: 20 per engine per arch. vep-rs: measured this sweep on both arches; fastVEP: s07, s08 measured this sweep on both arches, the other cells reused from sweep-20260918T224520Z; Perl VEP: s07, s08 measured this sweep on both arches, the other cells reused from sweep-20260918T224520Z. Total enumerated clone manifest: 208.
per_cell_aggregates_note: One row per (engine, arch, suite, condition): median, IQR (p25/p75), P5/P95, min, max across the 20 cross-instance samples for that cell, read from the median_of_20 rows of manuscript/data/wall_times.csv. Rows with reused=true were measured under the sweep their own source_sweep_id names and are carried forward unchanged: fastVEP's s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s05m, s06, s06m cells from sweep-20260918T224520Z; Perl VEP's s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s06 cells from sweep-20260918T224520Z.
perl_multisample_note: Perl VEP was not timed in the genotype-carrying condition in this campaign; every headline throughput cell runs the sites-only input (bcftools view -G). A single probe run of --fork 16 on the 3202-sample 1kg_highcov_chr21_multisample input on r8gd.8xlarge completed in 2,681 s with a container cgroup memory.peak of 25,323 MiB (manuscript/data/perl_bench.csv, dated 2026-09-18); it is one run, not a median of 20, and Table S8 omits Perl VEP for that reason.

pointer_suites.s09: SV real-world GRCh37; annotated inside the s07 run, so its wall-time row is a pointer (0 s).
pointer_suites.s10: SV real-world GRCh38; annotated inside the s08 run, so its wall-time row is a pointer (0 s).

provenance_sha_note: This sweep ran via run_clone_measurement.sh, so its dataset pin is the rolled dataset_inventory_sha256_<engine>_<arch> values above, one digest per clone over the staged vcf, caches, reference and ground_truth trees, NOT the per-artifact perl_cache_sha256 / json_cache_sha256 / fasta_sha256 / input_vcf_sha256s fields that single-host run_concordance.sh runs emit. Their absence here is the harness's designed behaviour, not an unpinned sweep.
public_build_inputs_note: Git object ids of the build inputs the binaries in this record were compiled from: the tree id of crates/ and the blob ids of Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and .cargo/config.toml, beside the sha256 of that Cargo.lock (the build ran --locked against it), and beside them the same ids crate by crate: measured_binary_crates are the tree ids of the crates the `vep` binary is built from (its dependency closure, dev-dependencies excluded), other_crates the tree ids of the workspace members outside that closure (separate binaries no closure crate depends on), and manifest_blobs the blob id of every crate's Cargo.toml. These are content-addressed, so a release tag carries the source of this build iff `git rev-parse <tag>:crates` and the three blob ids equal the values here, or, when a crate outside the closure has moved, iff every measured_binary_crates id, every manifest_blobs id and the three blob ids equal the values here: a change confined to non-manifest files of an other_crates member cannot reach the binary. The per-arch binary md5s in this record identify the binaries that were measured, not a value a rebuild reproduces: a --locked release build of the same inputs on the same toolchain yields a different digest run to run, so the md5 is checked against the archived binary, never against a rebuild.
reproduction_verdict: 40/40 fresh vep-rs clones completed, self-reported OK and self-terminated; every vep-rs clone measured all 10 timed cells plus both pointer suites; inventory parity exact across both arches; zero non-zero engine exits across 400 warmup and 400 timed vep-rs rows and across the 160 fastVEP and 160 Perl VEP rows measured here; no unstable cells. fastVEP and Perl VEP were measured on s07, s08 in this sweep (40 clones each) and their other cells carry forward from sweep-20260918T224520Z with ingested median_of_20 rows on both arches.
reuse_note: vep-rs was measured this sweep on 20 fresh clones per arch covering every timed cell on both arches; no vep-rs sites-only cell is carried over. fastVEP: s07, s08 measured this sweep (20 fresh clones per arch); its other cells (s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s05m, s06, s06m) are read from sweep-20260918T224520Z; Perl VEP: s07, s08 measured this sweep (20 fresh clones per arch); its other cells (s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s06) are read from sweep-20260918T224520Z. The suites measured this sweep for those engines are the ones whose inputs differ between the two campaigns (selective_remeasurement lists every timed input's digest in each), and every reused cell carries an ingested median_of_20 row on both arches.
reused_sweep_gates_note: Quality gates of the campaigns whose cells are reused here, one entry per campaign, read from that campaign's own record: nonzero_exit_rows counts engine invocations that exited non-zero across its warmup and timed rows, and unstable_cells lists cells whose P95/P5 ratio exceeded outlier_threshold_p95_p5_ratio. This record's own nonzero_exit_rows and unstable_cells cover the cells measured in this sweep, so the two together cover every cell in per_cell_aggregates.

selective_remeasurement.reason: The two campaigns differ on the structural-variant inputs and on nothing else: the synthetic 07_cnv_repeat file on both assemblies (each <CNV:TR> record sits on a tandem repeat the reference carries; its reference output is that set's own) and the GRCh38 1000 Genomes structural-variant file (sites-only, its eight fixed columns; its reference output is identical between the sets), so every structural-variant cell of every engine is measured in this sweep. The eight SNP and indel inputs, the engines, the image, the caches and the SNP and indel reference outputs are the same in both campaigns, so the comparators' SNP and indel cells are read from the earlier one.
selective_remeasurement.snp_indel_inputs_note: Object metadata of the eight SNP and indel inputs every clone stages (etag, size, last-modified): each object's last-modified date precedes both campaigns' launch, so the reused cells and this sweep's cells staged the same bytes.
selective_remeasurement.sv_input_digest_note: sha256 of each timed structural-variant input (the canonical_inputs of the ground-truth set each campaign staged), per assembly; a file whose two digests differ is listed in changed_inputs with what changed, read from the set's own provenance.

1kg_sv_chr21.change: sample columns absent; reference output identical

selective_remeasurement_note: fastVEP and Perl VEP measured s07, s08 in this sweep and are read from sweep-20260918T224520Z on every other suite. The two campaigns differ on the structural-variant inputs and on nothing else: the synthetic 07_cnv_repeat file on both assemblies (each <CNV:TR> record sits on a tandem repeat the reference carries; its reference output is that set's own) and the GRCh38 1000 Genomes structural-variant file (sites-only, its eight fixed columns; its reference output is identical between the sets), so every structural-variant cell of every engine is measured in this sweep. The eight SNP and indel inputs, the engines, the image, the caches and the SNP and indel reference outputs are the same in both campaigns, so the comparators' SNP and indel cells are read from the earlier one. The inputs that differ are GRCh37/07_cnv_repeat, GRCh38/07_cnv_repeat, GRCh38/1kg_sv_chr21, listed with both campaigns' digests in selective_remeasurement.sv_inputs; every other timed input carries the same digest or, for the SNP and indel inputs, an object last modified before either campaign (selective_remeasurement.snp_indel_inputs). The vep-rs dataset-inventory digest is 15c55e95 in this sweep against 387f0f48 in sweep-20260918T224520Z: the roll covers the structural-variant ground-truth tree and its canonical inputs, which is where the two campaigns differ.
sites_only_note: The six SNP and indel timed cells run sites-only inputs (bcftools view -G where the source VCF carried genotypes) for cross-engine fairness: VEP annotates per position and allele, so genotypes cannot change a consequence set, while every engine spends time parsing genotype columns it ignores. The two structural-variant cells annotate the archived per-file inputs as they are, every one of the 32 files sites-only (the GRCh38 1000 Genomes set is its eight fixed columns, and its reference output is identical between the two campaigns; selective_remeasurement.sv_inputs). The genotype-carrying cost is measured separately for vep-rs and fastVEP (the with_gt cells) and probed once for Perl VEP (perl_bench.csv).
spec_match_note: The two instance types (r8gd.8xlarge ARM, r8id.8xlarge x86) are spec-matched at 32 vCPU / 256 GiB / local NVMe instance store so the ARM-vs-x86 comparison isolates the CPU architecture. No Perl row of wall_times.csv carries peak_rss_mb; the Perl memory figures on record are the single-run container cgroup memory.peak probes in manuscript/data/perl_bench.csv (1kg_highcov_chr21_sites_only, 1kg_phase3_chr21_sites_only, clinvar_full_grch38_sites_only, gnomad_v4.1_chr21_sites_only, --fork 16, sites-only inputs), whose maximum is 17.7 GiB on gnomad_v4.1_chr21_sites_only, so the 256 GiB class is headroom above the timed sites-only cells rather than a requirement they measured. On the genotype-carrying 1kg_highcov_chr21_multisample input (3202 samples) the same probe on r8gd.8xlarge peaked at 24.7 GiB.
speedups_note: Geometric mean, minimum and maximum over the six SNP and indel suites (s01 to s06) of the per-cell vep-rs-vs-engine ratios (engine median over vep-rs median), sites-only, per architecture, computed from per_cell_aggregates. The SV cells (s07/s08) are excluded from the headline geomean and reported separately in speedups_sv, because their per-VCF, 16-invocation execution model is not comparable to the single-pass SNP and indel cells; every engine runs them at --fork 16, so the SV ratios are like-for-like on the invocation. Perl medians in these ratios are sweep-20260918T224520Z (s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s06) and sweep-20260920T012411Z (s07, s08); fastVEP medians are sweep-20260918T224520Z (s01, s02, s03, s04, s05, s05m, s06, s06m) and sweep-20260920T012411Z (s07, s08).
stability_note: No cell breached the P95/P5 <= 1.3 threshold. The widest spread among the 16 sites-only vep-rs cells measured this sweep is 1.124 (vep_rs x86_64 s05); across all 56 cells recorded in this file, the reused fastVEP and Perl VEP cohorts included, the maximum observed is 1.124 (vep_rs x86_64 s05).
